query: A 73-year-old man with a past medical history significant for high blood pressure, hypothyroidism, and diabetes presents to the outpatient clinic. He complains of joint pain, muscle pain, and fatigue that has been present for the last several weeks. On examination, you notice a butterfly-shaped rash across the bridge of his nose and cheeks. He has a blood pressure of 124/72 mm Hg and heart rate of 64/min. Of the following, which medication is most likely responsible for his presentation?
